name: Kedarnath kapat opening and closing
when: Opening late April–May; closing on Bhai Dooj, late October–November (dates set by the temple calendar)
summary: Twice a year the doors of Kedarnath change hands between summer and winter. In spring the Panchmukhi doli of Kedarnath travels up from its winter seat at Ukhimath to open the shrine; after Diwali it returns downhill with drums and pilgrims walking behind.
body: Kedarnath sits at 3,583 m and is snowbound for half the year, so the deity spends winter at the Omkareshwar temple in Ukhimath. The date for the spring opening is announced at Ukhimath on Mahashivratri, after priests consult the almanac. The temple doors close each year on Bhai Dooj, two days after Diwali. Badrinath's own date is announced separately at the Narendra Nagar palace on Basant Panchami.

The opening is a walk, not a single ceremony. The silver Panchmukhi doli leaves Ukhimath a few days before the date and halts at Guptkashi, Phata and Gaurikund, with villagers lining the road with flowers and offerings. On the last day it is carried up the 16–17 km path to Kedarnath, and the doors open at dawn in the presence of the Rawal, the chief priest, and the first pilgrims of the season.

Closing reverses the journey. After the morning puja on Bhai Dooj the doli is carried down in a single day to the lower halts and on to Ukhimath, where winter worship continues until spring. Yamunotri and Gangotri close around the same time, and Badrinath a couple of weeks later. Dates follow the Hindu calendar and shift every year; check current status before you travel.
tips: Avoid the opening week itself unless the ceremony is your reason for going; queues, registration checks and room prices all peak.
To see the doli without the summit crowd, wait for it at Guptkashi or Phata on its way up, or at Ukhimath when it returns in November.
Nights at Kedarnath in late April and early November fall well below freezing; carry a down jacket, gloves and a warm cap.

faqs.a: The date is announced at the Omkareshwar temple in Ukhimath on Mahashivratri, usually in February or March. In recent years Kedarnath has opened between late April and mid-May. Register for the yatra only once the date is out, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When does Kedarnath close for winter?
faqs.a: The doors close on Bhai Dooj, two days after Diwali, which falls in late October or November. The doli then travels down to Ukhimath, where the deity is worshipped through winter at the Omkareshwar temple.

faqs.q: Can tourists watch the kapat opening at Kedarnath?
faqs.a: Yes, anyone registered for the yatra can be at Kedarnath on opening day, but the crowd is large and the night before is very cold. Watching the doli pass Guptkashi, Phata or Gaurikund is easier and just as close to the ritual.

faqs.q: Where can I worship Kedarnath in winter?
faqs.a: At the Omkareshwar temple in Ukhimath, about 40 km from Gaurikund by road and open all year. Many pilgrims combine it with Chopta and Tungnath, whose own deity winters at Makkumath.

name: Ganga Dussehra, Rishikesh and Haridwar
image_query: Ganga Dussehra Har Ki Pauri Haridwar
when: May–June, on the tenth day of the bright half of Jyeshtha (lunar)
summary: Ganga Dussehra marks the day the river Ganga is said to have come down from heaven to earth. In Rishikesh and Haridwar lakhs of pilgrims bathe at the ghats, float leaf-boat lamps at the evening aarti and give alms. It falls in late May or June, in the hottest weeks of the year.
body: Hindu tradition holds that King Bhagiratha's penance brought the Ganga down from heaven to free the souls of his ancestors, and that she descended on the tenth day of the bright fortnight of Jyeshtha. The festival is called Dussehra, from das, ten, because a bath on this day is believed to wash away ten kinds of sin. Some temples hold ten days of ritual leading up to it.

Haridwar, 25 km south of Rishikesh, takes the largest crowds, with the ghats around Har Ki Pauri packed from before dawn. Rishikesh is calmer: pilgrims bathe at Triveni Ghat and at the steps below Parmarth Niketan and Swarg Ashram, and the evening aarti at both ghats is larger than usual. Upstream, the Gangotri temple marks the day with its own worship, close to where Bhagiratha is said to have meditated.

For visitors, the day is a chance to see the river at the centre of local life. Expect heat of 35–40 °C, closed roads around the main ghats and full hotels in Haridwar. Traffic diversions for the Char Dham yatra run at the same time. The date follows the lunar calendar; check current status before you travel.
tips: Stay in Rishikesh and visit Haridwar's Har Ki Pauri early in the morning, then retreat before the midday heat and the largest crowds.
If you want to bathe, use ghats with chains and lifeguards; the current is strong in June when snowmelt raises the river.
Buy leaf-boat diyas from ghat-side sellers rather than plastic offerings, and leave footwear at the stands provided.

faqs.a: It falls on the tenth day of the bright half of Jyeshtha in the Hindu calendar, usually late May or June. The exact date changes each year, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Rishikesh or Haridwar better for Ganga Dussehra?
faqs.a: Haridwar's Har Ki Pauri is the main bathing ghat and takes the biggest crowds. Rishikesh, 25 km upstream, is calmer, with bathing at Triveni Ghat and a larger evening aarti at Parmarth Niketan. Many visitors stay in Rishikesh and visit Haridwar early in the morning.

faqs.q: Is it safe to bathe in the Ganga on Ganga Dussehra?
faqs.a: Bathe only at ghats with chains, rails and lifeguards, and do not go beyond them. The river runs fast and cold in June from Himalayan snowmelt, and drownings happen every year. Keep children by the hand.

faqs.q: Do hotels get full on Ganga Dussehra?
faqs.a: Haridwar fills up, and Rishikesh is busy because the festival falls in Char Dham season and school holidays. Book a week or two ahead and expect higher weekend rates.

name: International Yoga Festival, Rishikesh
image_query: International Yoga Festival Rishikesh Parmarth Niketan
when: Early March, usually a week starting around 1 March
summary: Every March, Parmarth Niketan ashram in Rishikesh hosts a week-long International Yoga Festival, with sunrise to evening classes from teachers of many yoga schools, talks, kirtan and the nightly Ganga aarti. It draws students from India and abroad and needs paid registration in advance.
body: Rishikesh has been a yoga town since long before it became famous worldwide, with ashrams such as Sivananda's Divine Life Society working here from the 1930s. The International Yoga Festival at Parmarth Niketan, on the Swarg Ashram bank below Ram Jhula, gathers that tradition into one week each March, when days are 13–28 °C and the river is clear.

A typical day starts before sunrise with meditation and asana, continues with parallel classes in different styles, from hatha and Iyengar-influenced alignment to kundalini and yoga nidra, and adds lectures on philosophy, Ayurveda and pranayama in the afternoon. Evenings end at the ashram's ghat for the Ganga aarti, followed by music and kirtan. Teachers come from Indian schools and from abroad; the line-up changes each year.

Registration is paid and usually covers classes, ashram meals and, in some packages, a room inside Parmarth Niketan. Rooms go early; many participants stay in Tapovan or Swarg Ashram and walk in. Dates and fees change each year, so check the organiser's official site and check current status before you travel.
tips: Register early if you want a room inside Parmarth Niketan; otherwise book a stay within walking distance of Ram Jhula.
Ashram rules apply on the campus: no alcohol, meat or smoking, and modest clothing.
Bring your own mat and a warm layer; mornings by the river in early March are around 12–14 °C.

faqs.q: When is the International Yoga Festival in Rishikesh?
faqs.a: It is held in the first week of March, usually starting around 1 March, at Parmarth Niketan. Dates and programme change each year, so check the organiser's official site and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Do beginners attend the Rishikesh yoga festival?
faqs.a: Yes. Several classes each day suit beginners, and you can choose sessions by style and level. Tell teachers about injuries and skip anything that hurts; talk to your doctor first if you have a medical condition.

faqs.q: How much does the International Yoga Festival cost?
faqs.a: Registration is paid, with packages for Indian and international participants that may include meals and an ashram room. Prices change each year; see the organiser's official site for current fees.

faqs.q: Can I visit the festival without registering?
faqs.a: The evening Ganga aarti at Parmarth Niketan's ghat is open to all and free. Classes and talks inside the festival are for registered participants.
